findings.description: The async retry_any.__ror__ flattens when `other` is a retry_all, merging its sub-retries into an OR group. That changes the meaning of the expression.
findings.rationale: Trigger: `(retry_if_a & retry_if_b) | retry_if_c` in the asyncio module, where the left side is a retry_all. The left operand goes to retry_any.__ror__ with other=retry_all, so it returns retry_any(A, B, C). The intended result is any(all(A, B), C). A retry that should require both A and B now fires when only A holds, so retries happen when they should not. The sync retry.py version checks isinstance(other, retry_any) correctly, so the two modules diverge.
